Source.label: Source record
Source.explain: What is actually in the conversation, before any interpretation.

Content.label: Content
Content.explain: What was said: concepts, claims, questions, tasks and other content nodes.

Argument.label: Relations
Argument.explain: Role-typed connections between content, each grounded in a quote.

Process.label: Inquiry process and state
Process.explain: Who did what (moves), and actor-relative stance and question-status histories.

Review.label: Extraction and review
Review.explain: How records were produced, checked, kept apart from bad output and confirmed.

Session.label: Coding sessions
Session.explain: Claude Code and Codex session records read as conversations with tasks.

Cross.label: Across conversations
Cross.explain: Brian's verbatim positions gathered from many graphs, linked and mapped by topic.

Elsewhere.label: Elsewhere or theory only
Elsewhere.explain: Named in the docs but owned by another repository, or not a record type yet.

nodes.label: Conversation
nodes.explain: One visible transcript (chat export, bridge capture, meeting or coding session) with its participants, ordered messages and a coverage note saying what was left out. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:27.

nodes.label: Participant
nodes.explain: A speaker in a conversation, with role user, assistant or other. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:12.

nodes.label: Message
nodes.explain: One visible turn: speaker, ordinal and exact text; the only thing quotes are checked against. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:18.

nodes.label: Anchor
nodes.explain: A quote with its message id and Unicode start and end offsets; it must equal the message text at those offsets. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:36.

nodes.label: Content node
nodes.explain: Something said, of kind concept, claim, question, hypothesis, method, example, goal, reference, task or work; not the same as an utterance. Source: docs/ontology.md:16.

nodes.label: Question
nodes.explain: A content node of kind question; whether it is open is recorded by question events, never by the node itself. Source: docs/ontology.md:20.

nodes.label: Task
nodes.explain: A unit of work an agent lists as open in a coding session; carries the same status events as a question, plus dropped. Source: docs/ontology.md:18.

nodes.label: Work
nodes.explain: A delivered product (a pull request, a commit) seen in a tool record of a coding session. Source: docs/ontology.md:18.

nodes.label: Relation
nodes.explain: A reified, grounded connection of one of 13 kinds (supports, challenges, answers, supersedes...) whose players are bound by role; it can itself be challenged. Source: docs/ontology.md:22.

nodes.label: Role binding
nodes.explain: One (role, ref) pair of a relation, such as premise -> a claim id. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:59.

nodes.label: Relation signature
nodes.explain: For each relation kind, the roles it must have and the node kinds each role may bind; checked by validate(). Source: docs/ontology.md:26.

nodes.label: Inquiry move
nodes.explain: An act by one participant (ask, clarify, challenge, retract, reframe ... 15 kinds) with inputs, outputs, the message it happened at and previous moves. Source: docs/ontology.md:44.

nodes.label: Inference family
nodes.explain: Optional label on a move: induction, abduction, deduction or unspecified; the seed leaves it unspecified on purpose. Source: docs/ontology.md:50.

nodes.label: Stance event
nodes.explain: One participant's stance (posits, endorses, questions, rejects, suspends, retracts) toward a target, at a message; content is never belief without one. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:92.

nodes.label: Question event
nodes.explain: A status change of a question or task (open, answered, resolved, deferred, superseded, reopened, dropped) by one actor, at a message. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:99.

nodes.label: Open-question agenda
nodes.explain: The view of which questions are still open for which actor, folded from question events; an assistant's answer does not close a user's question. Source: src/inquiry_graph/views.py:23.

nodes.label: Grounded record and review status
nodes.explain: Every semantic record carries anchors, an origin (explicit or inferred) and review status proposed, confirmed or rejected; extraction output is always proposed. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:43.

nodes.label: Extraction record
nodes.explain: How a graph's annotations were produced: method, provider, model, prompt version and notes. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:110.

nodes.label: Candidates
nodes.explain: The proposed nodes, relations, moves and events from one extraction, before they are ingested into a graph. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:118.

nodes.label: Inquiry graph
nodes.explain: The canonical JSON record: conversations, all records, extractions and notes; written exclusively, never silently replaced. Source: src/inquiry_graph/model.py:126.

nodes.label: Quarantine
nodes.explain: The private folder where a failed extraction's raw response and error go, so bad output never replaces a graph. Source: src/inquiry_graph/io.py:177.

nodes.label: Coding session
nodes.explain: A Claude Code or Codex .jsonl session normalized into a conversation; prompts from headless runs are given to an automation participant. Source: src/inquiry_graph/coding_session.py:104.

nodes.label: Launch kind (typed or automated)
nodes.explain: Whether a person or a program typed a session's prompts, read from Claude Code entrypoint and Codex originator values. Source: src/inquiry_graph/coding_session.py:31.

nodes.label: End-of-reply fields
nodes.explain: The Session goal, Active subgoals, Done and Need anything from human lines an agent ends each reply with, read into tasks and question events. Source: src/inquiry_graph/coding_session.py:41.

nodes.label: Closure word
nodes.explain: The fixed word in 'Closed: <item> (<word>)' that maps to a task status (done -> resolved, put off -> deferred ...). Source: docs/ontology.md:18.

nodes.label: Resume digest
nodes.explain: Per session: goals, open, unknown-status and closed items, delivered work and requests waiting on Brian. Source: src/inquiry_graph/coding_session.py:244.

nodes.label: Brian position
nodes.explain: A stance or question event whose actor and anchored speaker are Brian and whose quote is verbatim in that message; the evidence unit agents ask for. Source: tools/ask_positions.py:4.

nodes.label: Cross-conversation link
nodes.explain: A judged pair of positions or questions Brian expressed in different conversations, proposed by embedding recall then a model judgment. Source: src/inquiry_graph/linker.py:40.

nodes.label: Positions topic map
nodes.explain: Brian's statements from chats and session prompts embedded and clustered into nested topics after the fact (topics are not stored on records). Source: wiki/index.md:29.

nodes.label: Topic name
nodes.explain: A short model-written name for one topic of the map, carried over between builds when the topic barely changed. Source: tools/name_topics.py:23.

nodes.label: Strategy episode
nodes.explain: A reusable reasoning strategy and its occurrences; not a record type: stored as method and example nodes joined by part_of and exemplifies. Source: docs/ontology.md:54.

nodes.label: Cross-source identity and conflict
nodes.explain: Deciding that records from different sources are the same thing, aligning them and detecting tension; owned by onto-canon6, which consumes these graphs. Source: docs/architecture/GOAL.md:48.

nodes.label: Warrant (support and defeat theory)
nodes.explain: A formal theory of when support beats challenge; moved to epistemic-warrant on 2026-09-29 and reached only through tools/warrant_adapter.py. Source: docs/architecture/GOAL.md:87.
